name: Nocturnal Hunger
description: Each opponent creates a Food token. Destroy target creature. If the gift wasn't promised, you lose 2 life.
assumptions: Treated node B (self, stack→gy) as ordinary post-resolution spell cleanup contributing no printed text, since there's no alternate destination for the resolved spell.
Read owner:"opp" on node C (no `target` flag present) as the schema's symmetric "each opponent" sense, rendering it "Each opponent creates a Food token."
Used the node order under root A ([B, C, D]) as the printed sentence order, placing the Food-token effect before the destroy/life-loss effect.

Grouped D and E into one continuous printed effect (not a separate paragraph) since D's own `to` field is "gy", not "stack" — the D→E step is a guaranteed, non-interrupting continuation of the same effect.
couldNotDerive: Whether the opponent's Food-token creation (node C) is itself optional / tied to a choice made when casting the spell — node C carries no `may` flag and no condition linking it to the "gift" referenced by node E's `cond:gift_not_promised` flag, so from the nodes alone it must be read as an unconditional, always-happens effect.

Whether the Food token goes to a single specific (promised/chosen) opponent or to every opponent symmetrically — node C's owner is "opp" with no `target` flag, which per schema reads as "each opponent," but nothing in the nodes represents a promise/choice mechanism that would narrow this to one opponent.
The Food token's own granted activated ability (e.g., a sacrifice-for-life rider) — the food registry entry supplies only labels/subtype, no ability text.
Any supertype or rarity, since the self registry entry supplies only manaCost and typeLine.
The card's name (withheld by design, not guessed).
notes: Real card (Nocturnal Hunger, confirmed via forge-model/data/nocturnal-hunger.txt's embedded Oracle text): {2}{B} Instant, keyword Gift a Food — 'You may promise an opponent a gift as you cast this spell. If you do, they create a Food token before its other effects.' / 'Destroy target creature. If the gift wasn't promised, you lose 2 life.' Mana cost and type line both matched exactly. The specific mechanic under retest — the LoseLife node's gift-conditional gate — is now correctly captured: node E carries 'qty:2 cond:gift_not_promised', the accurate translation of SVar:DBLoseLife's ConditionPresent$ Card.Self+PromisedGift | ConditionCompare$ EQ0 (giftGateFact's EQ0→'gift_not_promised' mapping), and the blind reconstruction rendered this as 'If the gift wasn't promised, you lose 2 life.' — a verbatim match to the real printed line. This confirms the fix: the previously-dropped condition on the generic LoseLife/GainLife/Draw fallback now round-trips correctly for this card, where the first attempt (see prior result.json revision) produced an unconditional 'You lose 2 life.' with no gift gating at all. One gap remains, and it is the pre-identified, deliberately deferred one: node C (Food-token creation, owner:'opp', no flags) still does not encode Gift's own 'may' choice or its single-opponent targeting. The real mechanic is optional (an as-you-cast choice, 'you may promise…') and resolves to one specific opponent (Forge's TokenOwner$ Promised), not an unconditional, symmetric 'each opponent creates a Food token' as owner:'opp' with no `target`/`may` flag reads under the current schema. Because node C has no `may` flag and no shared binding/condition tying it to node E's 'gift' state, the blind reconstruction necessarily produced 'Each opponent creates a Food token' as an unconditional effect rather than the real optional, single-target gift. This is a decomposition gap in how K:Gift's own token-creation choice is captured (the keyword still has no dedicated handler beyond the generic token-creation path), separate from and not undone by this round's LoseLife fix — which is the mechanic this retest was specifically checking, and which now checks out.
